<Quartier> is <one sentence placing it: borough, what bounds it>. This report compares every
francophone public elementary school in it: <N inside> whose building lies inside the quartier
as the city draws it, and <N edge> just outside its boundary within 300 m, marked † throughout.
For each school it shows the school itself, the kilometre around its building on the same
metrics as a school report, and the three-bedroom homes listed near it this month. It is one
output of MTL-101, which works backwards from the school to the neighbourhood.

::: {.callout-important}
## Not a ranking

Each zone metric is shown with its decile among the <N> francophone public elementary schools on
the island outside the West Island, marked [d1]{.decile-low} to [d3]{.decile-low} for the lowest
three tenths, [d4]{.decile-mid} to [d7]{.decile-mid} for the middle, and [d8]{.decile-high} to
[d10]{.decile-high} for the top three. A high decile means a high value, nothing more, so the
column header says which way is favourable for a family: ▲ higher is favourable, ▼ lower is
favourable, and columns with no glyph are descriptive. In the ▲ and ▼ columns the most
favourable school is [shaded]{.best}. The report computes no composite score and names no best
school; the IMSE is a socioeconomic index of the pupils enrolled, not a measure of academic
performance.
:::

# The schools

<!-- paste tbl-overview from report_tables.py --layout rows -->

The MEQ's IMSE decile (1 = most advantaged, 10 = most disadvantaged; 8 to 10 is the official
*milieu défavorisé*) is built from the enrolled pupils' parents' education and employment, not
from test results, and it can differ from the census figures for the residents of a school's
kilometre: <one sentence on where the two agree or diverge in this quartier and why (choice
programs, edge schools drawing from the next quartier)>. Program and admission come from the
project's hand-checked table; "unknown" means no page has been checked yet, not a regular
program.

::: {.callout-tip}

# The kilometres compared

Every row is the circle of one kilometre around that school's building, a stand-in for the
catchment polygon that exists only in the service centre's finder and PDF maps. The *<Quartier>*
row is computed over the whole polygon, and the island median over all <N> in-scope schools.

::: {.callout-warning}
## What these two datasets cannot say

The city states the incident file is not official SPVM statistics; positions are moved to the
nearest intersection and 17% of incidents have no coordinates and are absent from the rates.
The collision extract ends in 2021; its last two years are pandemic years. Both are rates of
reported events, not of risk. The quartier row has no victims-within-500-m figure because that
metric is defined from a school door.
:::

# Sources and caveats

- **Area**: Ville de Montréal, *Quartiers sociologiques* <or agglomeration limits>, opened on
  <date>; schools within 300 m outside the polygon included as edge schools.
- **School facts**: MEQ school points and *Indices de défavorisation* (school year <year>);
  program and admission from the project's `data/schools_programs.csv` as of <date>; no
  per-school web research in this report.
- **Zone tables**: `scripts/zone_stats.py` on open data fetched between <oldest> and <newest>
  (Ville de Montréal, Données Québec, INSPQ, Statistics Canada 2021 Census; métro and REM
  stations from OpenStreetMap contributors); dissemination areas by centroid, <min> to <max>
  per school kilometre and <n> for the quartier; IEMV coverage <x>%; tax bills matched for
  <y>% of units. Census 2021 is five years old; assessed values reflect the July 2024 market.
- **Listings**: as seen on <sites> on <date>.
- **Deciles**: among <N> in-scope schools, from `data/derived/zone_stats_all.parquet`.

# Conclusion

Four readings across the quartier, in the order a parent weighs them. Each states what the
tables show, not a verdict.

**School.** <Which schools carry a volet and how they admit; the IMSE spread across the quartier
and what the brief says about it; any school with an existing full report (@tbl-overview).>

**Safety.** <Where the crime and walk-to-school columns cluster, which kilometres differ, the
datasets' limits (@tbl-safety).>

**Livability.** <Children and households with children across the kilometres; the composite
indices; parks and métro access; the edge schools' other quartier (@tbl-people, @tbl-indices,
@tbl-parks).>

**Affordability.** <The stock, the assessed values and bills across the quartier against the
island, and what the listings found this month say (@tbl-stock, @tbl-cost, @tbl-for-sale,
@tbl-for-rent).>
